# A strict-quota convex family with nonuniform optimal geometric-mean buffers

This is an exact actual-body limitation of uniform small-buffer inference. All proper closed-minor quotas are strict. Nevertheless, for every sufficiently small epsilon there is an attained positive affine-multiplier optimum whose middle physical buffer stays bounded away from zero as epsilon tends to zero. The original body satisfies OC with a strict margin. Thus this is not a below-target obstruction.

The only ordinary dependencies are projective energy: E_K is continuous on K, vanishes on its boundary, is positive inside, satisfies E_K<=|K| with equality at the centroid, and E_K^(1/d) is concave. These were proved in the archived energy sources. The defining buffered cap formula and elementary strip estimates below give all required depth and parameter continuity; no regular-cap assumption is imposed.

## 1. Actual compatible fibers, masses, and quotas

Use bases P={0,1,2} in Z and planar fibers

    A=[−1/2,1/2]^2,
    K=conv{(1,0),(−1/2,2/3),(−1/2,−2/3)},
    B=[−1/20,1/20]^2.

They have areas 1,1,1/100 and common centroid zero. The actual midpoint (A+B)/2 is the square [−11/40,11/40]^2. It lies strictly inside K: its left edge is to the right of −1/2, and the two sloping support inequalities of K are

    |x_2| <= (4/9)(1−x_1).

At the square's right corners, 11/40<29/90. Therefore the convex hull of the three marked fibers has exactly these three integer fibers and has nonempty ambient interior.

The total mixed area is M=201/100 and the occupied parity count is k=2. Each singleton mass is strictly below M/2=201/200. The only two-point proper closed minors are {0,1} and {1,2}; both have two occupied parities and mass strictly below M. The subset {0,2} is not closed. Hence EVERY proper closed minor satisfies the strict mass quota V(T)<k(T)M/k.

## 2. Exact ordinary deepest base

At an endpoint base, a finite sufficiently steep integer tilt isolates any chosen continuous cap of its fiber. Thus its mixed depth equals its ordinary depth. The square A has ordinary maximum 1/2, uniquely at its symmetry center. For any other point y, a cut normal to y captures strictly less than half the square.

At every point of K, one of its three vertex-isolating caps has area at most 4/9: a largest barycentric coordinate is at least 1/3. A sufficiently steep positive integer tilt makes A empty and B full while retaining this K trace. Consequently the mixed depth at every middle point is at most

    4/9+1/100=409/900<1/2.                                 (1)

The B endpoint maximum is 1/200. Hence the unique ordinary deepest point is (0,0), with raw depth 1/2. It lies over an exposed endpoint of the base, despite all the strict quotas.

This is safely above the OC target

    (Gamma_2/2)M=67/150<1/2.

## 3. Invariant norm and geometric-mean multipliers

The within-fiber covariance is diagonal:

    Sigma_11=25001/241200,
    Sigma_22=170009/2170800.

Indeed A has covariance diag(1/12,1/12), K has diag(1/8,2/27), and B has diag(1/1200,1/1200); weight by the actual areas and divide by M. In particular

    1/16<lambda_min(Sigma)<=lambda_max(Sigma)<1/4.           (2)

Parameterize every positive affine multiplier on [0,2] by a ratio r>1/2:

    ell_1=r ell_0,        ell_2=(2r−1)ell_0.

Weighted geometric-mean normalization is

    ell_0^100 ell_1^100 ell_2=1,

so

    ell_0=[r^100(2r−1)]^(−1/201).                          (3)

For r>1, ell_0 strictly decreases and both ell_1 and ell_2 strictly increase. All three equal 1 at r=1. For r<=1, ell_0>=1. As r tends to infinity, ell_0 tends to zero and ell_1,ell_2 tend to infinity.

At a source (p,y), a cap with continuous normal u has its threshold shifted outward by

    epsilon (ell_p E_{K_p}(y)/M)^(1/3) sqrt(u^T Sigma u).   (4)

Pure integer caps are unchanged. Let Q_epsilon(r) be the maximum resulting raw buffered depth over the actual mixed set. Define

    tau_i=epsilon (ell_i/M)^(1/3).

The energy factor E_{K_i}(y)^(1/3) is not included in tau_i.

## 4. Exact minimax by a crossing, with all directions retained

Let A_epsilon(r) be the maximum buffered depth at base 0 and C_epsilon(r) that at base 1. Base 2 has buffered depth at most its isolating pure-integer mass 1/100, for every multiplier and every marked point.

Endpoint isolation implies that A_epsilon(r) is its own-fiber buffered depth maximum. That maximum is attained at the square center. Here is a direct reason: E_A^(1/3) is even and concave. For each fixed continuous normal, the condition that its buffered containing cap have mass at least q is a convex inequality in y (the quantile condition is u.y−tau_0 E_A(y)^(1/3)||u||_Sigma <=constant). The intersection over normals is convex and centrally symmetric. Whenever nonempty it contains zero. This also proves the claim without assuming that the maximizing ordinary normal remains fixed.

At zero, E_A(0)=1. For a Euclidean unit u, write delta=tau_0 sqrt(u^T Sigma u). The square contains the radius-1/2 disk. If tau_0<=1/2, then delta<=1/4 by (2), and every section at a height between −delta and 0 has length at least 1/2. Every square section has length at most sqrt(2)<2. Therefore

    1/2+tau_0/8 <= A_epsilon(r) <=1/2+tau_0.               (5)

More precisely the same section bound on nested strips shows that this maximum is STRICTLY increasing in tau_0 throughout that small interval. Thus for r>=1 and epsilon<=10^(−4), A_epsilon(r) is continuous, strictly decreasing, lies below 1/2+epsilon, and tends to 1/2.

For a middle mark y, retain an ordinary K cap of area at most 4/9 and isolate A empty, B full by a sufficiently steep integer tilt. Buffering moves the K threshold by at most tau_1 E_K(y)^(1/3)/2. Since diam(K)<2, this gives the exact uniform bound

    b_epsilon(1,y)<=409/900+tau_1 E_K(y)^(1/3)
                     <=409/900+tau_1.                   (6)

The middle maximum C_epsilon(r) is nondecreasing in ell_1. It is continuous: changing tau_1 changes every normalized continuous threshold by at most |Delta tau_1|/2, uniformly in y because E_K<=1. Each of the three fiber cap changes is bounded by its diameter times this shift. Taking infima over all tilted normals and then maxima over y preserves this common Lipschitz bound. Pure integer caps do not change.

At r=1, (6) yields C_epsilon(1)<1/2 when epsilon<=10^(−4). Conversely if tau_1>=4, then at the K centroid the shift is at least 1 in every Euclidean unit continuous direction, by (2). Since K is contained in the unit disk, every such cap contains its whole K fiber, of mass 1. Pure integer caps through base 1 have mass at least 101/100. Hence

    tau_1>=4  implies  C_epsilon(r)>=1.                   (7)

For r>1 the middle tau_1 increases without bound. By continuity there is a first finite crossing r_epsilon>1 such that

    A_epsilon(r_epsilon)=C_epsilon(r_epsilon)=q_epsilon.   (8)

This crossing is a GLOBAL multiplier minimizer. Before it, A_epsilon is strictly larger. After it, C_epsilon is no smaller. Values r<=1 have A_epsilon(r)>=A_epsilon(1)>q_epsilon. The tiny endpoint never competes. Thus no unproved optimizer attainment or cap smoothness enters this conclusion. A later flat interval of equally optimal multipliers is not excluded or needed.

At this actual positive optimum both bases 0 and 1 have buffered deepest points, whereas only base 0 was originally deepest. The square center is one of them, and a middle maximizing mark exists by the standard compact buffered-level argument (or continuity of the same cap-quantile superlevels).

## 5. Quantitative escape and nonvanishing ACTUAL buffer

At the first crossing, (5) and (8) imply

    1/2<q_epsilon<1/2+epsilon.

Using (6) at a middle maximizing mark y_epsilon and (7) gives

    41/900 <=tau_1 E_K(y_epsilon)^(1/3)<=tau_1<4.           (9)

Consequently

    M(41/900)^3 epsilon^(−3)<=ell_1<64M epsilon^(−3).      (10)

Also 1<ell_2/ell_1<2 and normalization gives

    ell_0=ell_1^(−1)ell_2^(−1/100).

Together these prove

    ell_1,ell_2=Theta(epsilon^(−3)),
    ell_0=Theta(epsilon^(303/100)),
    tau_0=Theta(epsilon^(201/100)),
    q_epsilon−1/2=Theta(epsilon^(201/100)).                (11)

The constants in these two-sided comparisons are independent of epsilon in the specified range and follow explicitly from (5), (9), and (10).

Most importantly, at the ACTUAL middle maximizing mark, not just at its centroid or at the level of a coefficient, (9) and (2) show that the outward threshold displacement in EVERY Euclidean unit continuous direction is at least

    41/3600.                                             (12)

Thus the optimized physical buffer does not vanish as epsilon tends to zero. An argument claiming uniform convergence back to ordinary deepest points would fail on this strict-quota family.

## 6. What this does and does not rule out

The example satisfies exact convex compatibility, positive planar fibers, strict no-heavy masses, every strict proper-closed-minor quota, and attained positive geometric-mean multiplier minima. It refutes the inference from those facts ALONE to uniformly small physical buffers.

Its optimized depth tends to the ordinary raw value 1/2, which remains strictly above the OC target 67/150. It therefore does not test a genuinely below-target attained family. A below-target hypothesis would need an additional argument if it is to exclude this escape mechanism.

Neither the arithmetic complement-face theorem nor its fixed-epsilon attainment application is contradicted. At the escaped parameter boundary, a middle base center can indeed acquire enough buffer to reach its base depth. The minimizing sequence stops at a finite nonzero physical displacement long before that boundary saturation.
